title: 高市首相、改憲に向け「決断のための議論進める」　反対集会やデモも
extracted_text: 憲法記念日の3日、各地で憲法改正を求める集会や、改憲に反対する集会・デモなどが開かれた。高市早苗首相（自民党総裁）は改憲を求める集会にビデオメッセージを寄せ、「国会において決断のための議論を進める」と述べ、改めて改憲に意欲を示した。ただ、具体的な項目や時期には触れなかった。 首相がメッセージを寄せたのは、保守系団体・日本会議が主導する「美しい日本の憲法をつくる国民の会」などが開いた集会で、自民と連立を組む日本維新の会のほか、国民民主党の玉木雄一郎代表らが出席した。 首相は憲法について「国の礎であり根幹」とし、「その価値を摩滅させないためにも時代の要請にあわせて本来定期的な更新が図られるべきだ」と強調。「政治家が国民の負託に応えるために行うべきなのは、決断のための議論だ」と述べた。 憲法改正をめぐり、安倍晋三首相（当時）は2017年、同集会へのメッセージで、9条への自衛隊明記などを掲げ、20年の新憲法施行への意欲を表明した。自民は18年に自衛隊明記を含む「改憲4項目」をまとめ、現在も維持しているが、首相は触れなかった。 集会では維新の阿部圭史衆院議員が、戦力不保持を定める9条2項を削除し、集団的自衛権行使の全面容認と「国防軍」の保持を主張。玉木氏は「9条を改正すべきだという立場に立っている」とし、2項を残しつつ自衛隊を戦力として位置づける案を掲げた。 首相はメッセージで改憲を目指す時期に触れなかったが、4月の自民党大会では「改正の発議にめどが立った状態で来年の党大会を迎えたい」と述べ、1年後の発議に意欲を示した。ただ、発議には衆参両院で3分の2の賛成が必要だが、与党は参院で過半数に満たずハードルは高い。 参政党の神谷宗幣代表は3日付の談話で「改憲そのものには賛成だが、日本の国益や反グローバリズムの観点から、内容を是々非々で判断していく」とした。 一方、東京・有明では「9条を壊すな！実行委員会」などによる護憲派の集会が開かれ、主催者発表で約5万人が参加した。立憲民主党の吉田忠智参院議員は「憲法を守り生かすために全力を挙げる。9条を含む平和憲法は世界に誇る日本の宝だ」、共産党の田村智子委員長は「自民は憲法に自衛隊を書き込むだけだと言うが、書き込めば（自衛隊の）海外派遣を阻止する力が打ち破られる」と訴えた。 衆院野党第1党の中道改革連合と、昨年自民との連立を解消した公明党は参加しなかった。それぞれ3日付の談話で中道は「憲法の基本原理を大切にし、権力の乱用を防ぐ立憲主義を堅持する」としつつ、「時代の変化にあわせて改憲論議を深めていくべきだ」とコメント。公明は「衆参両院における憲法論議の積み重ねを踏まえつつ、憲法の新たな可能性に対して真摯（しんし）に向き合う」とした。 「戦争反対」「高市政権は憲法を守れ」。国会前や各地で、憲法9条改正に反対するデモが行われています。「時は来た」と、改憲に突き進む高市政権の思惑と、9条が果たしてきた役割などを考えます。
translated_text: On May 3rd, Constitution Day, various gatherings calling for constitutional revision were held across the country, as well as gatherings and demonstrations opposing revision. Prime Minister Sanae Takachi (LDP President) sent a video message to a gathering calling for revision, stating, 'We will proceed with discussions for decision-making in the Diet,' once again expressing her determination to pursue constitutional revision. However, she did not touch on specific items or timing. The Prime Minister's message was delivered at a gathering organized by conservative groups including the 'National Association for Creating a Beautiful Japanese Constitution,' led by the organization Nippon Kaigi. Other attendees included the Japan Innovation Party, which forms a coalition with the LDP, as well as Democratic Party for the People Representative Yuichiro Tamaki. The Prime Minister referred to the constitution as 'the foundation and cornerstone of the nation,' emphasizing that 'to prevent its value from eroding, it should undergo regular updates in response to the demands of the times.' She stated, 'What politicians should do to fulfill the public's trust is to engage in discussions for decision-making.' Regarding constitutional revision, then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe sent a message to the same gathering in 2017, expressing his determination to achieve a new constitution by 2020, including the explicit mention of the Self-Defense Forces in Article 9. In 2018, the LDP compiled 'four revision items' including the explicit mention of the Self-Defense Forces, which it maintains to this day, but the Prime Minister did not refer to them. At the gathering, House of Representatives member Asei Abe of the Innovation Party advocated deleting Paragraph 2 of Article 9, which prohibits the maintenance of war potential, and called for the full acceptance of the exercise of the right to collective self-defense and the maintenance of a 'National Defense Force.' Representative Tamaki stated, 'We maintain the position that Article 9 should be revised,' presenting a plan to retain Paragraph 2 while positioning the Self-Defense Forces as a military force. Although the Prime Minister did not mention a timeline for pursuing revision in her message, at the LDP convention in April she stated, 'I want to welcome next year's party convention with a clear prospect for initiating revision,' expressing her determination to initiate it within one year. However, passage requires a two-thirds majority in both houses of the Diet, and the ruling party lacks a majority in the upper house, making the hurdle high. On the 3rd, Representative Soken Kamiya of the Sanseitoparty stated in comments, 'I support revision itself, but will judge the content on a case-by-case basis from the perspective of Japan's national interests and anti-globalism.' Meanwhile, in Tokyo's Ariake area, a pro-constitution gathering was held by groups including 'Don't Destroy Article 9! Executive Committee,' with approximately 50,000 participants according to the organizers. Democratic Party of the House of Representatives member Tadatomo Yoshida stated, 'I will devote my full effort to protecting and preserving the constitution. The peace constitution, including Article 9, is Japan's treasure that the world can be proud of.' Japanese Communist Party Chairman Tomoko Tamaru stated, 'The LDP says it will simply write the Self-Defense Forces into the constitution, but once written, the power to prevent overseas dispatch of the (Self-Defense Forces) will be broken.' The primary opposition party in the House of Representatives, the Central Reform Union, and Komeito, which dissolved its coalition with the LDP last year, did not participate. In their comments on the 3rd, the Central Reform Union stated, 'We cherish the basic principles of the constitution and will uphold constitutionalism to prevent abuse of power,' while adding, 'We should deepen discussions on revision in line with changes in the times.' Komeito stated, 'We will sincerely engage with new possibilities for the constitution based on the accumulation of constitutional discussions in both houses of the Diet.' 'Oppose War,' 'The Takachi Administration Must Protect the Constitution.' Demonstrations opposing the revision of Article 9 of the constitution are being held in front of the Diet and across the country. 'The time has come.' We consider the intentions of the Takachi administration pushing ahead with revision and the role that Article 9 has played.
title_en: PM Takachi Proceeds with 'Discussions for Decision-Making' Toward Constitutional Revision - Opposition Gatherings and Demonstrations Also Held
